A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CodePercept, ICC-1M, and STEM2Code-Eval. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable matching. The absence of v1 Figures 7–10 from v2 is a document change, not an extraction gap.

before.justification: v1 reports original scaling experiments, benchmark evaluations, quantitative ablations, training curves, and qualitative reconstruction results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical evaluations and ablations, including Appendix G, and adds two result rows to Table 1.

M1.justification: The three data-generation pipelines, caption refinement, explanatory code supervision, and SFT-to-GRPO training procedure remain unchanged. The new PAMI-labelled result rows do not document any algorithmic or architectural modification.

E1.justification: Both versions retain ICC-1M training, the six reasoning benchmarks, and the 1,000-example STEM2Code-Eval benchmark. The added Table 1 rows use existing benchmark columns; removing illustrative galleries does not establish changed dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Removing v1 Figure 7 eliminates the qualitative comparison of Direct Image-to-Code Generation against Description-Enhanced Image-to-Code Generation. The named external MLLM baseline sets in the quantitative tables remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The documented captioner-solver pairings, benchmark sizes, scoring procedures, training budgets, and execution checks are unchanged. No revised settings accompany the new PAMI-labelled rows, so their underlying experimental differences cannot be inferred.

E4.justification: v2 removes Figure 7's six-example comparison testing whether description conditioning improves reconstruction. The quantitative pipeline, caption-grounding, and joint-training ablations in Table 3, the Appendix C caption case study, and Figure 5 training curves remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed variation, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional result rows retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds CodePercept-8B-S1-PAMI and Caption-32B-S1-PAMI, averaging 66.55 and 68.84 under Qwen3-30A3-Thinking. The original 63.32 and 67.30 rows remain. These are additional, unexplained variants rather than verified same-setting improvements. Tables 2–5 retain their values, while Figure 7's qualitative reconstruction outputs disappear.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, equations, GRPO objective, and advantage calculation retain the same content. No assumptions, propositions, proofs, or mathematical corrections are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims that perception bottlenecks STEM reasoning, executable code improves perception through two complementary tasks, and STEM2Code-Eval provides reconstruction-based assessment. The wording edits do not materially alter these contributions.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning perception versus reasoning, caption-code complementarity, hallucination reduction, and solid-geometry difficulties remain unchanged. No substantive limitation, applicability qualification, or mechanism explanation is added or revised.

D1.justification: The implementation section and Appendices A–F retain the same prompts, hyperparameters, hardware, data-construction instructions, evaluation implementation, and code-access link. No implementation details are supplied for the new PAMI-labelled entries.

R1.justification: v2 adds MathCanvas and MathCoder-VL to the related-work citations and bibliography. These are limited additions to the existing STEM-model discussion, without substantive repositioning or corresponding new baseline evaluations.

P1.justification: v2 revises author, affiliation, and contact information, adds acknowledgements, trims a repetitive related-work passage, and makes small wording edits. Implement Details becomes an unnumbered paragraph, with subsequent experiment subsections renumbered; the overall narrative is retained.

P2.justification: v2 removes the entire concluding visualization suite: Figure 7's reconstruction comparisons, Figures 8–9's seed-and-variant galleries, and Figure 10's solid-geometry examples. This substantially reduces the visual presentation of the data pipelines. Table 1 gains rows, Tables 2–3 move, Figure 1's caption is shortened, and page-number footers disappear.

improvement.justification: The limited citation and prose updates are outweighed by lost qualitative supporting evidence and unexplained new results. Table 1's new 32B row reports 68.84 with a +2.7 annotation, although the listed baseline is 64.63, a difference of 4.21. Undefined PAMI variants and inconsistent annotations weaken reporting clarity. The central method and retained quantitative evidence remain intact, limiting the overall decline.
